# Stream fixtures

The parity harness for the streamed turn (#126). Each `<name>.sse` is an SSE body a
fake gateway serves; `<name>.golden.json` is what the app must observe when it drives
that body through `HermesSession` with its own wait → poll loop.
`android/app/src/test/java/com/hermesvox/core/StreamParityTest.kt` replays every
fixture and fails on any difference; the replay machinery itself is
`StreamReplay.kt`, shared with `RouteParityTest` (the cross-route proof).

The goldens were generated by the Go voice core (`tools/streamdump`, removed with the
Go code) and the Kotlin core matched all of them before the Go code was deleted. They
are the frozen specification of the streaming behaviour: change one only on purpose,
in its own commit, saying why.

## Format

Optional directive lines come first, then the body, served verbatim with a flush
after each line:

| directive | effect |
|---|---|
| `#! voice` | start the first turn with `voiceTurn` (the voice prefix rides the input) |
| `#! hold` | after the body, keep the connection open until the client closes it; the golden records whether it did (`held_connection_closed`) |
| `#! idle_timeout_ms N` | shrink the stream idle watchdog to N ms for this fixture |
| `#! cancel_after_events N` | barge in (`cancelStream`) once N events have been polled |
| `#! stored JSON` | answer non-streaming requests with JSON and run the /compress script: turn, `turnStored("/compress")`, turn |
| `#! route runs` | serve the turn on the `/v1/runs` route: `POST /v1/runs` → 202 `{run_id}`, then `GET /v1/runs/run_parity/events` carries the fixture body. Default is `responses`. |

The golden records every event, the poll snapshot at each deterministic point (the
done poll; the poll before a barge-in), the cancel semantics, and every request the
gateway saw (method, path, bearer, scope header, Accept on streamed turns, model,
input, stream flag, `previous_response_id`).

## Where they came from

| fixture | source |
|---|---|
| `normal` | `TestStreamStateRacePollDrain` (sent as a voice turn) |
| `error` | `TestStreamFailedSurfacesReason` (mid-stream `response.failed`) |
| `timeout` | `TestStreamIdleWatchdog` (idle watchdog, 150 ms) |
| `barge` | `TestCancelStreamRetiresMapEntry` (cancel retires the stream, closes the connection) |
| `compress` | `TestTurnStoredRidesTheStreamedChain` (H2: /compress rides the streamed chain) |
| `commentary`, `framing`, `incomplete` | `stream_contract_test.go` |
| `tools` | built from the event shapes documented in the Go `stream.go` (function_call / function_call_output) |
| `malformed` | synthetic decoding edge cases: wrong-typed fields, `null` payloads, folded keys, lenient JSON, raw arguments, lone surrogates |
| `runs-*` | **hand-built from the gateway source**, not captured: Hermes v0.22.6 `gateway/platforms/api_server_runs.py` (`_run_event`, `_execute_run`'s `_text_cb` / `_interim_cb` / `_make_run_event_callback`, `_FIXED_EVENT_FIELDS`, `terminal_run_status`, `_handle_run_events`) and `_approval_request_event` in `api_server.py`. The two-request shape (202 admission + `/events` SSE) and the event fields are the source's; the prose is invented to pair with an existing responses fixture. No gateway was reachable when these were written. |

`runs-*` fixtures are the `/v1/runs` vocabulary and exist for the cross-route proof:
`RouteParityTest` replays each pair (e.g. `commentary.sse` and `runs-commentary.sse`)
and asserts both produce the same rendered turn. The wire names are translated to the
app's vocabulary in `core/Stream.kt` (`dispatchRun` / `normalizeRunEvent`); the
goldens here pin the translated shapes, exactly like the responses fixtures.

`tools.golden.json` pins a quirk inherited from Go: the answer delta after a tool
output is appended to the `[tool-done]` marker line, so the done poll's `text` is
empty. It is recorded, not endorsed.

## Adding a fixture

1. Write `testdata/stream/<name>.sse`.
2. Run the parity test with `STREAM_GOLDEN_UPDATE=1`; it writes goldens that are
   missing and never overwrites an existing one:

   ```sh
   cd android
   STREAM_GOLDEN_UPDATE=1 ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest --tests '*StreamParityTest'
   ```

3. Read the new golden line by line. It was produced by the code under test, so it is
   only a specification once a person has checked it against the gateway's behaviour.
4. Commit the fixture and the golden together.
